definitions.gloss: kokuji; a kanji invented in Japan
definitions.explanation: A character made in Japan in the style of Chinese characters but not found in Chinese, such as {峠|とうげ} or {畑|はたけ}. Many have only a kun'yomi and no on'yomi.

examples.japanese: {峠|とうげ}は{国字|こくじ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Tōge is one of the kokuji.

examples.japanese: {国字|こくじ}には{音読|おんよ}みがないものが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many kokuji have no on'yomi reading.

examples.japanese: {畑|はたけ}や{峠|とうげ}など、{日常|にちじょう}でよく{目|め}にする{漢字|かんじ}の{中|なか}にも{国字|こくじ}がある。
examples.english: Among the kanji we see every day, such as hatake and tōge, there are also kokuji.

notes:
A character made in Japan in the style of Chinese characters but not found in Chinese — for example {峠|とうげ}, {畑|はたけ}, and {働|はたら}く. Many {国字|こくじ} have only a kun'yomi (native reading) and no on'yomi.

COMMON EXAMPLES:
- {峠|とうげ}: mountain pass
- {畑|はたけ}: dry field
- {込|こ}む: to be crowded

USAGE:
{国字|こくじ} can also mean a nation's own writing system, but the 'Japanese-made kanji' sense is the usual one.
